risks.note: BRSR flags cane as an integral and essential part of the manufacturing process whose timely availability depends on climate and other conditions like pricing; financial implication indicated as negative. Company states the risk is not under control and mitigates only by maintaining production and manufacture of other by-products.

BRSR lists change in Government policies on FRP as a risk with negative financial implication; mitigation is to follow Government guidelines and focus on co-generation and by-products. MD&A adds that FRP rose Rs.15 to Rs.355/quintal for SY2026 (10.25% basic recovery) and Karnataka SAP rose Rs.250/quintal, while MSP has not been revised since 2019 (industry urging revision to Rs.39/kg) - a squeeze between rising input cost and a frozen output floor price.
risks.risk: Government policy changes, particularly on cane FRP and administered sugar pricing

risks.note: BRSR environmental issues row: changes in rainfall patterns, temperatures and extreme weather events can affect crop yields and quality; negative financial implication. MD&A corroborates - Maharashtra and Karnataka saw reduced yields from early sugarcane flowering due to excess rain and shorter harvest windows.
risks.risk: Climate change and adverse weather affecting crop yield and quality

risks.note: BRSR: the company is situated on the banks of the Krishna River with the Hippergi barrage nearby and sufficient water is normally available, but in a drought situation there is a shortage of water. Mitigated through effective water management practices; financial implication negative.
risks.risk: Water availability / drought exposure at the plants

risks.note: BRSR: sugar production requires a timely and continuous supply of good quality cane which may be affected by improper farmer engagement. Mitigated through cordial relations with farmers and an R&D cell plus field staff visiting farmers for cultivation guidance and yield enhancement.
risks.risk: Farmer engagement dependency for continuous cane supply

risks.note: BRSR flags poor labour practices as a credibility and high-turnover risk with negative financial implication. MD&A adds that human labour constitutes 52% of total sugarcane cultivation cost, so any change flows directly into cost of cultivation; increased farm mechanisation is cited as the offset.
risks.risk: Labour practices, farm labour cost and attrition

risks.note: MD&A: in October 2024 the Supreme Court upheld States' power to regulate industrial alcohol, which may give state governments the ability to tax it. Material because Industrial Alcohol is the single largest revenue line at 44.66% of turnover.
risks.risk: Regulatory/taxation risk on industrial alcohol after the Supreme Court ruling

risks.note: MD&A: with 5 million tonne opening stock, total domestic availability of 33.00 million tonne exceeds consumption of 28.00 million tonne, and ISO expects a global surplus of 1.625 million tonnes for 2025/26. India is likely to ship only 7.5-8 lakh tonnes in the 2025-26 season, well short of the quota, as weak global price parity discourages outbound sales; international raw sugar fell to $313/MT in Feb 2026 from $445/MT a year earlier. The company itself did not export any sugar during the year and does not export directly.
risks.risk: Sugar oversupply and weak export parity
